questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below does **not** have an inverse?

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 10 & 4\end{aligned}],\,S=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 10 & 0\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $R$, we have

$$
det(R)=5\cdot 4-10\cdot 2=0.
$$

Because $det(R)=0,$ we conclude that $R$ is not invertible.

- The matrix $S$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix. So, it is not invertible.

- For the matrix $T$, we have

$$
det(T)=2\cdot 2-(-2)\cdot 2=8.
$$

Because $det(T)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $T$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $R$ and $S$ do not have an inverse.

questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below does **not** have an inverse?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 15 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- The matrix $A$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix. So, it is not invertible.

- For the matrix $B$, we have

$$
det(B)=-3\cdot 5-1\cdot 15=-30.
$$

Because $det(B)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $B$ is invertible.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
det(C)=7\cdot 2-3\cdot 4=2.
$$

Because $det(C)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $C$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $A$ does not have an inverse.

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Variable in a Singular Matrix
questions.problem: If $A=[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 27 & k\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value(s) of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $A$ is singular if and only if $det(A)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =k\cdot k-27\cdot 3 \\  & ={k}^{2}-81.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{k}^{2}-81 & =0 \\ {k}^{2} & =81 \\ k & =\pm 9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the values of $k$ are $k=\pm 9.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Variable in a Singular Matrix
questions.problem: If $M=[\begin{aligned}t & 5 \\ t & 9\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value(s) of $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $M$ is singular if and only if $det(M)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =t\cdot 9-t\cdot 5 \\  & =9t-5t \\  & =4t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4t & =0 \\ t & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $t$ is $t=0.$

questions.problem:
If $B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 7x-3 & x+8\end{aligned}]$
is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$

{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is singular if and only if $det(B)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =4\cdot (x+8)-(-2)\cdot (7x-3) \\  & =4x+32+14x-6 \\  & =18x+26.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}18x+26 & =0 \\ 18x & =-26 \\ x & =-\frac{13}{9}\end{aligned}
$$
